## Part 2: Data Ethics

**Scenario:** The fertilizer trial you just analyzed (Fert1, Fert2, Fert3 vs. plant height) was conducted on a small family-run farm that agreed to host the experiment on their land. The farm has used its own traditional, informally-developed fertilizer blend for generations and agreed to let a university team test it against two commercial fertilizers, expecting the results would help them decide what to use going forward.

After the trial, the university researchers find that the commercial fertilizer significantly outperforms the farm's traditional blend. The results are written up for publication and shared with an agricultural input company that helped fund the study, with the goal of marketing the winning fertilizer more broadly. The farm family is not listed as a co-author, is not consulted on how the results are described, and does not know the data will be shared with the company. The publication does not mention that the "traditional blend" recipe itself — knowledge developed and refined by the family over decades — is now effectively public and attributable to no one.

Consider this scenario as you answer the following questions.
